cases.description: A token decoder disables JWT signature verification while an independent audit-event paginator returns one fewer item than its documented limit.

pull_request.title: Decode access tokens and page audit events
pull_request.body: The access_token is supplied by an untrusted client and must have its HS256 signature verified with signing_key before sub is trusted. page_events must return exactly limit items whenever that many remain after offset.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+import jwt
+
+def subject_from_access_token(access_token, signing_key):
+    claims = jwt.decode(access_token, options={'verify_signature': False})
+    return claims['sub']

@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
+def page_events(events, offset, limit):
+    return events[offset:offset + limit - 1]

expected_findings.description: Decoding the untrusted access token with signature verification disabled lets a caller forge the subject claim.
Subtracting one from the exclusive slice end returns at most limit minus one audit events instead of the documented limit.

cases.description: A password-reset code is generated with the deterministic general-purpose random module instead of a cryptographically secure source.

pull_request.title: Generate password reset codes
pull_request.body: A caller who knows a code can reset the corresponding account password. Attackers may request reset codes for accounts they do not own, so generated codes must be cryptographically unpredictable; rate limiting is enforced separately.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+from random import Random
+
+_rng = Random()
+def create_password_reset_code():
+    return f'{_rng.randrange(1_000_000):06d}'

expected_findings.description: The general-purpose random generator is predictable and is not suitable for password-reset credentials that grant account access.

cases.description: A bearer access token is placed in a callback URL query parameter where normal URL handling can disclose it.

pull_request.title: Build the browser callback URL
pull_request.body: The access token parameter, access_token, is a bearer credential that grants account API access. The returned URL is opened by the user's browser and may be recorded in browser history, reverse-proxy logs, analytics, and Referer headers.

expected_findings.description: Putting the bearer token in the query string exposes it through browser history, logs, analytics, or Referer propagation.

cases.description: A password-reset helper generates a high-entropy token and stores only its digest while unchanged caller code owns expiry and one-time-use enforcement.

pull_request.title: Create password reset tokens safely
pull_request.body: The unchanged caller sends the returned token over TLS and enforces a fifteen-minute expiry plus one-time use. store_digest persists only the supplied digest. This helper is responsible only for generating an unpredictable token and storing its digest.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,8 @@
+import hashlib
+import secrets
+
+def new_password_reset_token(store_digest):
+    token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
+    digest = hashlib.sha256(token.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()
+    store_digest(digest)
+    return token
